answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehaviour, like a bridge toll that makes crossing expensive. A newcomer must post collateral and build verifiable work history before gaining full trading rights, so creating thousands of fake agents means funding thousands of stakes. A cipher-signed reputation record ties each agent's past deals to one key, and peers standing on the same knoll of shared history can spot a fresh clone with no record and refuse it until it earns trust through costly, honest work.
